column3: Uses mouth and lip imagery for the opening and its border.
Repeats the hem and the phrase “all around,” rather than compressing them to a single description.
Repeats “a gold bell and a pomegranate” twice rather than summarizing them as alternating plural objects.
The coming in and going out are joined by “and” rather than “or.”
Repeats the making instruction for the tunics, sashes, and headdresses rather than using one verb for the list.
“Fill their hand” retains the hand image rendered “ordain them.”
“His seed after him” retains the seed image and the following relation rather than simply “his descendants.”
